vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: unhuman
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle describes a legitimate domain management tool that interacts with unhuman.domains and supports Bitcoin payments via an agent-wallet. It uses standard npm package installation and explicitly warns the AI agent to confirm with the user before initiating financial transactions using the `--wallet` flag. While the skill involves managing sensitive data (domain management tokens, wallet keys) stored locally, there is no evidence of intentional data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or deceptive prompt injection against the agent. Potential shell injection via the `dns set` command is a vulnerability in how an agent might construct arguments, not an indicator of malicious intent within the skill definition itself.

llm.summary: The skill matches its domain-management purpose, but it uses unpinned npm commands for sensitive domain and Bitcoin-wallet operations.

dimensions.detail: Those unpinned packages would run with the user's local permissions while the workflow may involve domain-control tokens, DNS changes, nameserver changes, recovery codes, and wallet access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata and examples use unpinned npm/npx package names for unhuman and agent-wallet, so the reviewed artifact does not fix the code version that will run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses domain changes, token recovery, stored management tokens, and explicitly says to confirm with the user before using the wallet payment flag.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent token and wallet storage under ~/.unhuman and ~/.agent-wallet is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it is sensitive and raises the impact of the unpinned execution model.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose is coherent: search, register, renew, and manage domains through unhuman.domains, including optional Lightning payment support.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only pinned, reviewed versions of the npm packages, keep domain-management tokens and wallet data isolated, and require clear user approval for registrations, renewals, DNS or nameserver changes, and any wallet-enabled payment.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The matched phrase about paying with bitcoin is part of the stated payment workflow; I found no artifact evidence of ransomware behavior, mass encryption, ransom notes, or destructive code.
[RP1] unexpected: The artifact repeatedly invokes unversioned npx commands for domain and wallet workflows; this is a material review concern because the operations affect domain control and real payments.
[T08] unexpected: The static scan's dependency concern is supported by the SKILL.md metadata and examples, which do not pin versions or integrity for the third-party packages.
